title: Tenant-aware burst fingerprinting and SLA proxying for mixed reserved pools
creator: Aisha Mehta
description: Problem: In mixed-tenant reserved GPU pools we need correct, auditable attribution of burst consumption and SLA credit adjustments while preserving low-latency enforcement. Current heuristics produce over-attribution for short-lived retries and client-side replays, causing surprise credits and incorrect billing. This ticket implements a tenant-aware burst fingerprinting system plus an SLA-proxying layer that allows temporary safe spillover to fallback capacity without immediately debiting tenant burst or SLA credits. Goals: 1) Accurate per-tenant burst attribution with <1% false-positive attribution on synthetic replay tests. 2) Real-time enforcement decisions that avoid blocking critical customer requests while preserving charge correctness for post-facto reconciliation. 3) Auditability and retroactive correction: event ledger allowing SLA-credit adjustments and customer-facing statements. Scope: fingerprint extraction on ingress, approximate in-line deduplication for enforcement, event-sourced ledger entries for every admission decision, and a small orchestration service that implements SLA proxying policies.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Fingerprinting implemented in ingress agents and verified across 3 workload patterns (steady, bursty, retry-heavy) with test harness. 2) Real-time enforcement route uses fingerprinting to avoid double-counting within fingerprint TTL and logs decision metadata to event ledger. 3) SLA proxying can route qualified overflow to fallback capacity and mark ledger entries as 'proxied' so billing can reconcile later. 4) End-to-end integration test that simulates client replays produces no more than 1% misattribution. 5) Documentation (Confluence) and open PRs merged; rollout gated by canary with metrics to Datadog dashboards.
design_decisions: - Chosen hybrid model: lightweight probabilistic fingerprinting + short TTL (60s) for real-time enforcement; event-sourced ledger for authoritative post-facto reconciliation. Alternatives considered: full event-only enforcement (too high-latency), pure stateless hashing (insufficient for replay identification). - Fingerprint components: tenant_id, model_hash, request_prefix_hash, timestamp bucket, and request-unique nonce if present. Use Murmur3 for speed. - Dedup window: default 60s with per-tenant tuning via config. - SLA-proxy policy: allow proxied admissions only if pool headroom < threshold AND request priority >= P1 (customer-configured). Proxied admissions are recorded but do not decrement immediate tenant burst balance; reconciler consumes or issues SLA credits later. - Data retention: ledger entries retained 90 days; aggregation metrics 13 months.
implementation_steps: 1) Add fingerprint extraction middleware to API gateway (work in ingress service branch). 2) Implement lightweight in-memory cache keyed by fingerprint for dedupe with LRU + expiry. 3) Add event emission for all admission decisions (accepted/ proxied/ rejected) to event stream (Kafka topic 'dedicated-burst-decisions'). 4) Build small reconciler microservice that consumes the stream and applies retroactive accounting (ledger writes, SLA crediting). 5) Add new DB schema for ledger rows (event_id, fingerprint, tenant, pool, decision, proxied_flag, consumed_tokens, timestamp). 6) Wire UI and audit logs in Console (route-level view) to display proxied counts and reconciler status. 7) Create canary rollout with a 10% tenant sample and Datadog monitors.
risks_and_mitigation: - Risk: Fingerprint collisions could under-attribute; mitigation: include multiple entropy components and test collision rate across production traces. - Risk: Real-time dedupe cache increases memory pressure on ingress; mitigation: bounded LRU and per-tenant sharding plus circuit-breaker to disable dedupe under memory pressure. - Risk: Customers may be confused by proxied admissions; mitigation: UI labels, customer-facing docs, and a grace reconciliation window with explicit notifications. - Risk: Latency regression; mitigation: microbenchmarks limit extra work per-request to <200us in 95th percentile.
testing_plan: - Unit tests for fingerprint generation with edge cases (missing tenant, long prefixes, nonce reuse). - Synthetic workload replay harness that replays recorded production traces with injected replays; measure attribution error. - Integration test: full flow API -> ingress dedupe -> event emits -> reconciler -> ledger writes. - Load test: measure ingress memory and 95th perc latency with dedupe enabled at 1M rps equivalent (scaled). - Canary: roll to 10% of tenants for 48h with metrics: proxied_rate, dedupe_hit_rate, reconciliation_lag, billing_adjustment_count.
monitoring_and_slos: - New Datadog dashboards: Dedicated/Burst/Fingerprint-Hits, Dedicated/Burst/Proxied-Rate, Dedicated/Burst/Reconciliation-Lag. - Alerts: reconciliation_lag > 5m (P1), proxied_rate > baseline+5% (P2), dedupe_cache_evictions > threshold (P2). - SLO: reconciliation lag 99th <= 2m for canary, <=10m at GA.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (dev): feature branch + unit/integration tests. Phase 2 (staging): synthetic replay tests and stress tests. Phase 3 (canary): 10% tenants for 48h; monitor metrics and customer support queue. Phase 4 (GA): 100% with soft-fallback disabled after 2 weeks if reconciler stable. Rollback: toggle ingress dedupe off and mark proxied mode disabled in orchestrator. Schedule: start canary 2026-03-20, GA target 2026-04-20.
open_questions: 1) How do we bill for proxied admissions if reconciler cannot reclaim capacity from fallback? (proposal: issue SLA credit to tenant proportional to proxied consumption). 2) Do we need tenant-level opt-out for proxied mode? PM request: yes for enterprise customers. 3) Exact ledger schema and cardinality constraints for high-traffic tenants. Engineering to propose final schema by 2026-03-05.
